The next big opportunity for sustainable cities may not be only how much clean power we generate, but how well we move it, manage it and deliver it.

The scale of opportunity is enormous. Global energy investment is set to reach US$3.3 trillion in 2025, with US$2.2 trillion flowing to clean energy technologies, including renewables, grids, storage and electrification. But that investment only delivers its full value if clean power reaches people, businesses and growing cities.

Cities are already home to 3.69 billion people, around 45% of the world's population, and account for 75% of global energy use and 70% of CO₂ emissions. As cities grow, demand from cooling, buildings, electric mobility, digital services and public infrastructure will make grids central to sustainable urban planning.

This is where grids become development infrastructure.

Modern, flexible and digital grids can connect more renewable energy, reduce outages, support electric mobility, power efficient buildings, enable cooling, strengthen water and sanitation systems, improve services in underserved communities, reduce reliance on diesel backup and unlock cleaner, more productive urban economies.

Around 3,000 GW of renewable energy projects were stuck in grid connection queues in 2023. Unlocking that power through better planning, digital systems, storage and grid investment could turn stranded clean energy into jobs, services and resilience.

By 2040, around 80 million kilometres of grids may need to be added or replaced, roughly equivalent to the entire existing global grid. This is one of the largest infrastructure opportunities of the energy transition.

For rapidly growing cities in Africa and Asia, grid investment can help avoid high-carbon lock-in and support a different urban future: cleaner air, reliable services, productive enterprises, safer streets, better cooling and more resilient communities.

As HLPF continues, the message is clear: SDG 7 and SDG 11 must be planned through the grid. Modern grids can turn clean energy ambition into sustainable urban transformation.
